review_notes: I read the whole file and compared the four base-vs-exponent limit lemmas (lines 55–93). I checked the `tendsto_const_mul_atBot_of_*` lemmas and the `log_pos` / `log_pos_iff` signatures. I also looked at `tendsto_log_mul_self_nhdsLT_zero`, which has a clunky proof. I did not flag it, because `continuous_mul_log` depends on it and I found no clearly simpler, verified replacement. I also considered the duplicated proofs of the two `IsBigO.mul_atTop_rpow*` lemmas and rejected that as a finding. The suggested replacement in the finding has not been compiled. It relies on `log_pos : 1 < x → 0 < log x`, which the sibling lemma at line 87 already uses.

findings.problem: The goal `0 < log b` is closed by going through `log_pos_iff`, which needs a side goal `0 ≤ b` discharged by `positivity`, and then an opaque `aesop` call for `1 < b`. The hypothesis `hb : 1 < b` is already in context, and `Real.log_pos` states exactly this implication. The sibling lemma `tendsto_rpow_atTop_of_base_gt_one` (line 87) uses `log_pos hb` for the same goal.
findings.benefit: It removes two automation calls (`positivity` and `aesop`) and one needless iff, so the reader sees directly that `1 < b` gives `0 < log b`. It also makes this lemma match the proof of `tendsto_rpow_atTop_of_base_gt_one`, and it is faster and less fragile than `aesop`.
